predecessors.note: The page infobox: Predecessor Gupta Empire. The gupta-empire dossier carries the Chhattisgarh forest kings in its 347 sphere (Mahakantara and the atavika rajas).

land.text: Bastar and Koraput, the core of the Nala kingdom (present-day Chhattisgarh and Odisha)

successors.note: The page: "An Aihole inscription credits Chalukya king Kirtivarman I with destroying the Nalas" (Kirtivarman I page: "the night of doom" for the Nalas; reign 566-592; Nalavadi "may have derived from its former rulers, the Nalas").

land.text: Bastar and Koraput, the core of the Nala kingdom (present-day Chhattisgarh and Odisha)

successors.note: The page: the Nalas "were probably supplanted by the Panduvamshi dynasty", and the Sharabhapuriyas "may also have contributed to their decline"; a branch "may have ruled a small area until the 7th or 8th century". No dossier for either successor yet.

capitals.name: Pushkari (Garhdhanora, Bastar)
capitals.note: The page: Pushkari, "identified with modern Garhdhanora in Bastar district" (Podagada in Koraput was once thought to be Pushkari); Skandavarman "re-populated the deserted city of Pushkari". The coordinates are the centre of Bastar, approximate to some 50 km; the page gives none.

correction.text: Bastar and Koraput, the core of the Nala kingdom (present-day Chhattisgarh and Odisha)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Nala row. The page gives no area: the core is "around Bastar and Koraput, in present-day Chhattisgarh and Odisha". The page dates the dynasty only to the 6th century; the Narendrasena page has the Nala king Bhavadattavarman invade Vidarbha around 445, so the kingdom must exist by then, and 440 is a bridge.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Bhavadattavarman's invasion "reached Vidarbha and took Nandivardhana" (the Vakataka former capital), held until the Vakataka recapture "around 445 CE". The years 443-444 are the researcher's bridge for an undated invasion.

keyframe_review.note: The Nala core again after the loss of Nandivardhana; the page says the Nalas "suffered reverses against the Vakatakas as well as the Chalukyas" and does not draw any change of frontier until the end.

region.text: Bastar and Koraput, the core of the Nala kingdom (present-day Chhattisgarh and Odisha)

ledger.note: c. 440: the Nalas hold Bastar and Koraput. The page dates the dynasty only to the "6th century" (infobox established and disestablished in it); the Narendrasena page puts the Nala king Bhavadattavarman at war with the Vakataka around 445, so the start is a bridge before that. Varaha-raja, known from gold coins, is "possibly the earliest king" but "not certain" to be the founder.

region.text: Nandivardhana (Nagardhan), the Vakataka former capital in Vidarbha

ledger.note: c. 443: Bhavadattavarman takes Nandivardhana. "an invasion by the Nala king Bhavadattavarman of Bastar" that reached Vidarbha and took Nandivardhana; the Nala page: Bhavadatta extended Nala territory into Vidarbha, "possibly at the expense of the Vakatakas". The year is not given; it is bridged before the recapture.

c. 445: Narendrasena retakes Nandivardhana. "Around 445 CE, during the final years of Kumaragupta I's reign" he retook Nandivardhana, "his former capital, by driving out joint Gupta and Nala forces"; the page says he may have sacked the Nala capital, without naming it. Narendrasena's reign is c. 455-480 on the same page, which does not square with a war in 445.

region.text: Bastar and Koraput, the core of the Nala kingdom (present-day Chhattisgarh and Odisha)

ledger.note: c. 580: Kirtivarman I destroys the Nalas. The Kirtivarman I page gives no year for the Nala campaign (the Aihole inscription calls him "the night of doom" for the Nalas; reign 566-592); 580 is the middle of his reign, a bridge. The Nala page gives only "6th century" and a small branch that "may have ruled a small area until the 7th or 8th century".

wars.name: Narendrasena's war against the Nalas
wars.outcome: The Vakataka king Narendrasena retakes Nandivardhana from joint Gupta and Nala forces around 445.
wars.note: The years 443-445 are the invasion (undated) and the recapture ("around 445 CE"). Narendrasena's reign on the same page is c. 455-480, so either the war was fought by his predecessor or the 445 date is wrong; the page says Skandagupta later recaptured Malwa from him.

certainty.note: No border is given; the Nala kingdom is Bastar and Koraput by name only.

notes: New state Cliopatria lacks (sa-02-d asks for it, 440-480 from the Narendrasena page). Three pages opened (budget 2-5). The pages disagree: the Nala page puts the dynasty in the 6th century, the Narendrasena page makes Bhavadattavarman a rival of the Vakataka around 445 (the same page gives Narendrasena c. 455-480). Both ends are bridges (confidence 1): 440 before the 445 war, 580 in the middle of Kirtivarman I's reign. Successors Panduvamshi dynasty and Sharabhapuriya dynasty have no dossier yet (sa-03). No ruler strip: only regnal years of single grants (Arthapati 7, Bhavadattavarman 11, Skandavarman 12). Gazetteer names needed: Bastar, Koraput (regions), Pushkari, Nandivardhana (used as radii).
